mainTopic: The final letters, the origins of the תרגום, דניאל's vision, and stopping Temple service and Torah study to hear the מגילה.
overview: This עמוד finishes the discussion of the final letters מנצפ״ך. They existed at Sinai, were forgotten, and the צופים only restored them, because a נביא may not add new laws. The גמרא then brings more teachings of רבי ירמיה (or רבי חייא בר אבא). אונקלוס הגר wrote the תרגום of the תורה, and יונתן בן עוזיאל wrote the תרגום of the נביאים. When יונתן translated the נביאים, the land shook, but he was not allowed to translate the כתובים, because they hide the time of משיח. The תרגום of the תורה existed in עזרא's time, was forgotten, and was restored by אונקלוס. The נביאים translation shook the land because it revealed hidden passages, as רב יוסף shows from a פסוק in זכריה. The same רבי ירמיה says the men with דניאל were חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי, which leads to רבינא's advice about sudden, unexplained fear. Finally, the גמרא returns to מגילת אסתר: even כהנים, לוים, and ישראל stop their Temple service to hear the מגילה, and בית רבי learn that תלמוד תורה is stopped too. The גמרא then questions whether Temple service is really greater than Torah study, using the story of יהושע and the angel, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The closed letters already existed at Sinai
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge. The closed ם and ס in the לוחות stood by a miracle, so they already existed at הר סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: They stood by a miracle! So these letters already existed at Sinai.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a challenge that started earlier. The ם and ס were carved all the way through the stone tablets, so their middle pieces could only stay in place by a miracle. That proves these closed letters existed at Sinai.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי ירמיה said the צופים (prophets) established the final letters מנצפ״ך. Here the גמרא pushes back. If the closed ם and ס were already on the לוחות, the prophets could not have invented them.

keyTerms.meaning: The stone tablets given at Sinai (mentioned in the lead-up to this line)
The letters ם and ס, which are fully closed shapes

steps.confusionAlert: This line is only the end of a sentence. The full statement, earlier, is: 'The ם and ס of the לוחות stood by a miracle!' The point is that a closed shape cut all the way through stone leaves a middle piece with nothing holding it up.

phrases.english: stood by way of a miracle!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a challenge begun earlier against the claim that the צופים established מנצפ״ך.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's claim that the צופים established the final letters.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The closed ם was already in the לוחות at Sinai, so the prophets could not have created it.

steps.title: Both forms existed, but their placement was unknown
steps.stepSummary: Both forms of each letter did exist. The people did not know which form belongs in the middle of a word and which at the end, and the צופים settled this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, both forms existed. But people did not know which one goes in the middle of a word and which at the end. The Seers came and set the rule: open forms in the middle, closed forms at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that both shapes existed at Sinai. The prophets' contribution was fixing where each shape is used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer changes what the prophets did. They did not invent new letters; they made a rule about placement. The open forms (מ, נ, צ, פ, כ) go in the middle of a word, and the closed or final forms (ם, ן, ץ, ף, ך) go at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: Open forms (the regular letters used in the middle of a word)
Closed forms (the final letters used at the end of a word)

phrases.english: Yes, they did exist,
but they did not know
which one is used in the middle of a word
and which one at the end of a word,
and the Seers came and established
the open forms in the middle of a word
and the closed forms at the end of a word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the לוחות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the prophets' role: they set placement rules rather than creating the letters.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The prophets invented the final letters, which seems impossible since ם existed at Sinai.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both forms existed, and the prophets only fixed which form goes in the middle and which at the end.

steps.title: Even fixing placement would be a new law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. The words אלה המצות teach that no prophet may add anything new, so how could the prophets even set placement rules?
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, though, the verse says 'These are the commandments.' That teaches that from now on no prophet may introduce anything new!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from the previous step. Setting where each letter goes is still a new rule, and prophets are not allowed to make new rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse אלה המצות (ויקרא כז:לד) is read as closing the תורה to additions by later prophets. Even a 'small' placement rule counts as adding to the תורה. So the previous answer has not really solved the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: 'These are the commandments' (ויקרא כז:לד), showing that the מצוות are complete

phrases.english: In the end, 'These are the commandments,'
which teaches that no prophet may
introduce anything new from now on!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the צופים established the placement of the letter forms.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Any rule a prophet adds is forbidden by אלה המצות, and that includes a placement rule.

steps.title: The forms were forgotten and later restored
steps.stepSummary: The final answer is that the placement rules were given at Sinai, forgotten over time, and restored by the prophets.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the people forgot them, and the prophets came back and re-established them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final resolution. The prophets did not create anything new; they brought back something that had been forgotten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Restoring a forgotten tradition is not 'adding' to the תורה, so it does not break the rule of אלה המצות. This answer protects both sides: the final letters come from Sinai, and רבי ירמיה can still credit the צופים with re-establishing them.

keyTerms.meaning: And they established them (here, re-established them)

steps.whatToRemember: The final letters מנצפ״ך come from הר סיני. The צופים only restored them after they were forgotten, because a prophet may not introduce a new law.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key principle: prophets cannot add to the תורה, but they can restore traditions that were lost.

phrases.english: Rather, they forgot them,
and then they went back and re-established them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from אלה המצות and closes the discussion of מנצפ״ך.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The final letters were given at Sinai, forgotten, and restored by the prophets. This is not a new law.

steps.title: אונקלוס wrote the Aramaic translation of the תורה
steps.stepSummary: Another teaching from the same אמורא: אונקלוס הגר composed the תרגום of the תורה based on what he learned from רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ירמיה said, and some say it was רבי חייא בר אבא: The translation of the תורה was said by אונקלוס הגר, from the mouths of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It brings another teaching from the same אמורא who taught about מנצפ״ך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'And said' links this to the earlier teaching of רבי ירמיה about the final letters. The point is that the standard Aramaic translation of the תורה, תרגום אונקלוס, comes from authentic חז״ל tradition, taught by רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: From the mouth of, meaning based on someone's teaching

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya said,
and some say it was Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba:
The translation of the Torah —
Onkelos the convert said it
from the mouths of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from the same אמורא, placed here because it follows his teaching about מנצפ״ך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תרגום אונקלוס on the תורה was composed by אונקלוס הגר based on the teachings of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.

steps.title: יונתן בן עוזיאל wrote the translation of the נביאים
steps.stepSummary: The same teaching continues: יונתן בן עוזיאל composed the תרגום of the נביאים based on a tradition from חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The translation of the נביאים was said by יונתן בן עוזיאל, from the mouths of חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי.
steps.whatsHappening: The same אמורא continues his teaching. Now he names who wrote the Aramaic translation of נביאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the tradition goes back further, to the last three prophets. That gives תרגום יונתן a source in prophecy itself. This sets up the dramatic reaction described in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Prophets (the second section of תנ״ך)
A leading student of הלל who wrote the translation of נביאים

phrases.english: The translation of the Prophets —
Yonatan ben Uzziel said it
from the mouths of Chaggai, Zechariah, and Malachi,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same teaching, moving from the תורה to the נביאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תרגום יונתן on the נביאים was composed by יונתן בן עוזיאל based on the tradition of חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי.

steps.title: The land quaked and a heavenly voice protested
steps.stepSummary: When יונתן בן עוזיאל revealed the meaning of the נביאים, ארץ ישראל shook over a huge area, and a בת קול asked who had revealed God's secrets.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ארץ ישראל quaked over an area of four hundred פרסה by four hundred פרסה. A בת קול came out and said: Who is this who revealed My secrets to people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about what happened when יונתן wrote his translation. The question from the heavenly voice sets up the next part, where יונתן answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earthquake shows that the translation revealed hidden meanings of the נביאים, not just their surface words. The בת קול's question is a protest, and the response comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A Persian mile, a unit of distance

phrases.english: and the Land of Israel quaked
four hundred parsa
by four hundred parsa.
A heavenly voice came out and said:
Who is this who revealed
My secrets to human beings?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the story of what happened when יונתן בן עוזיאל wrote his translation, and leads into his answer next.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Revealing the hidden meaning of the נביאים caused an earthquake and a heavenly protest.

steps.title: יונתן בן עוזיאל explains why he translated the נביאים
steps.stepSummary: יונתן בן עוזיאל admits he revealed the hidden meanings of the נביאים. He insists he did it for God's honor, to prevent arguments in ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: יונתן בן עוזיאל stood up and said: I am the one who revealed Your secrets to people. You know clearly that I did not do it for my own honor or for my family's honor. I did it for Your honor, so that arguments would not multiply in ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: יונתן בן עוזיאל answers the בת קול's question from the last step. He openly says he did it and explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not deny revealing God's secrets. He defends his reason instead. Without a clear translation, people would argue over what hard פסוקים in the נביאים mean, so his תרגום was meant to bring unity, not personal fame.

keyTerms.meaning: He stood up on his feet, to respond publicly and with respect
Your secrets, meaning the hidden meanings of the נביאים
It is revealed and known before You, meaning You know my true intentions

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד יוֹנָתָן בֶּן עוּזִּיאֵל עַל רַגְלָיו
phrases.english: Yonatan ben Uzziel stood up on his feet
and said: I am the one who revealed
Your secrets to mankind.
It is revealed and known before You
that I did not do it for my own honor,
and not for the honor of my father's house,
but rather I did it for Your honor,
so that disputes would not multiply in Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמַד יוֹנָתָן בֶּן עוּזִּיאֵל עַל רַגְלָיו וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the בת קול's question in step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תרגום of the נביאים was revealed only for God's honor, to prevent arguments in ישראל.

steps.title: A בת קול stops the translation of the כתובים
steps.stepSummary: יונתן בן עוזיאל wanted to translate the כתובים too, but a בת קול told him: Enough!
steps.simpleTranslation: He also wanted to reveal a translation of the כתובים. A בת קול came out and said to him: It is enough for you!
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. יונתן בן עוזיאל tries to translate the כתובים, but Heaven stops him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His translation of the נביאים was allowed after his explanation, but the כתובים are treated differently. The גמרא does not give the reason yet. That comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Writings, the third section of תנ"ך
It is enough for you, stop here

phrases.english: And he also sought to reveal
a translation of the Writings,
a Divine Voice came out and said to him:
Enough for you!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד בִּיקֵּשׁ לְגַלּוֹת תַּרְגּוּם שֶׁל כְּתוּבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the יונתן בן עוזיאל story with a new attempt
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven did not allow a תרגום of the כתובים to be revealed.

steps.title: Why was the translation of the כתובים stopped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason the בת קול stopped him.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the story to ask why the כתובים could not be translated. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נביאים were also full of secrets and were still allowed. So the גמרא wants to know what makes the כתובים different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a תרגום of the כתובים was forbidden

steps.title: The כתובים contain the time of משיח
steps.stepSummary: The כתובים hold hidden hints to when משיח will come, so a clear translation would reveal it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it contains the end-time of משיח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The כתובים could not be translated because they hide the time of משיח's arrival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ספר דניאל, which is part of the כתובים, hints at the time of the redemption in a coded way. A clear תרגום would expose that date to everyone, and Heaven wanted it kept hidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The end-time, when משיח will come

steps.whatToRemember: The נביאים were translated by יונתן בן עוזיאל, but the כתובים were not, because they hide the time of משיח.

phrases.english: Because it contains the End of the Messiah.
phrases.notes: This mainly means ספר דניאל, which hints at when the redemption will come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כתובים contain the hidden time of משיח, which must not be revealed.

steps.title: Did the תרגום of the תורה already exist in עזרא's time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim in step 5 that אונקלוס הגר wrote the תרגום of the תורה. רב reads a פסוק in נחמיה as showing a תרגום already existed in the days of עזרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did אונקלוס הגר really compose the תרגום of the תורה? But רב איקא בר אבין said in the name of רב חננאל, who said in the name of רב: What does this פסוק mean, 'They read in the book, the Torah of God, clearly, and gave the sense, and helped them understand the reading'? 'They read in the book, the Torah of God' is the text itself. 'Clearly' is the תרגום. 'And gave the sense' is the division into פסוקים. 'And helped them understand the reading' is the טעמים. Some say it is the מסורות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier teaching about אונקלוס and attacks it. It uses a פסוק from the days of עזרא, which is long before אונקלוס lived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב explains that the word מפורש in the פסוק refers to the Aramaic תרגום read along with the תורה in עזרא's time. If a תרגום already existed then, אונקלוס, who lived much later, could not have been the one who composed it. The rest of רב's reading, about פסוקים, טעמים, and מסורות, is part of the same quoted teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't so-and-so say? This opens a challenge from another source
Clearly explained, read here as the תרגום
The division of the text into verses
The cantillation notes, which also show how the words are grouped
The traditions about how each word is spelled and written

steps.confusionAlert: Only the word מפורש (the תרגום) creates the challenge. The other parts of the פסוק (פסוקים, טעמים, מסורות) are simply the rest of רב's explanation and do not add to the attack.

phrases.english: And the translation of the Torah,
did Onkelos the convert compose it?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב אִיקָא בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Ika bar Avin say
that Rav Chananel said that Rav said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"And they read in the book, the Torah of God,
clearly, and they gave the sense,
and they caused them to understand the reading" (Nehemiah 8:8).
"And they read in the book, the Torah of God": this is the scriptural text;
"clearly": this is the translation;
"and they gave the sense": these are the verse divisions;
"and they caused them to understand the reading": these are the cantillation notes,
and some say: these are the Masoretic traditions!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַרְגּוּם שֶׁל תּוֹרָה, אוּנְקְלוֹס הַגֵּר אֲמָרוֹ? וְהָא אָמַר רַב אִיקָא בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the יונתן בן עוזיאל story and returns to challenge the אונקלוס teaching from step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 5 that אונקלוס הגר composed the תרגום of the תורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב reads מפורש in נחמיה 8:8 as the תרגום, which shows a תרגום existed in עזרא's time, long before אונקלוס.

steps.title: The translation was forgotten and restored
steps.stepSummary: The old תרגום from עזרא's time was forgotten, and אונקלוס re-established it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They forgot it, and then it was re-established.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Both statements are true: the תרגום existed in עזרא's time, was later forgotten, and אונקלוס brought it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אונקלוס did not invent the תרגום. He restored an ancient one that had been lost. This removes the contradiction between רב's reading of the פסוק and the teaching about אונקלוס.

keyTerms.meaning: And they went back and re-established them

steps.whatToRemember: The תרגום of the תורה goes back to עזרא's time. It was forgotten, and אונקלוס restored it. This is the same pattern used earlier for the placement rules.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the exact answer the גמרא gave in step 4 about the placement rules. Its message is that ancient traditions can be lost and later restored, without anyone inventing something new.

phrases.english: They had forgotten it, and then they went back and re-established it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical reconciliation: the source was lost and later restored
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that אונקלוס composed a brand-new תרגום, which contradicts its existence in עזרא's time
steps.terutzMaskana: The ancient תרגום was forgotten, and אונקלוס re-established it

steps.title: Why did only the translation of the נביאים shake the land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the land quaked when the נביאים were translated, but not when the תורה was translated.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference? Why did the land not shake over the translation of the תורה, but it did shake over the translation of the נביאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that compares the two translations. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that the land of ישראל quaked when יונתן בן עוזיאל translated the נביאים. Now that we know אונקלוס also translated the תורה, the גמרא asks why that translation caused no quake. Both are translations, so why the different reaction?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (asks why two similar cases are treated differently)

phrases.english: What is different about that of the Torah
phrases.notes: The translation of the תורה by אונקלוס

phrases.english: that the land did not quake
while over that of the Prophets it quaked?
phrases.notes: The translation of the נביאים by יונתן בן עוזיאל

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that step 13 confirmed אונקלוס translated the תורה, the גמרא compares his translation with the translation of the נביאים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did one translation cause the land to quake and the other did not?

steps.title: The תורה is clear, but the נביאים have hidden passages
steps.stepSummary: The meaning of the תורה is already clear. The נביאים contain some unclear passages, so translating them exposed hidden meaning. A פסוק in זכריה is given as an example.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the תורה, the meaning is clear. In the נביאים, some things are clear and some things are hidden. For example, it says: 'On that day there will be a great mourning in ירושלים, like the mourning of הדדרימון in the valley of מגידון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תורה translation revealed nothing new, but the נביאים translation explained hidden passages. It then quotes a confusing פסוק as an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quake was a reaction to secrets being revealed. The תורה's translation only restated what people already understood, so there was nothing to react to. The translation of the נביאים opened up passages that had been unclear until then.

keyTerms.meaning: A name in the פסוק whose meaning is unclear without the תרגום

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the תורה has no deep secrets. It means the plain meaning of the תורה's words is clear, so translating it did not expose anything hidden.

phrases.english: In the Torah, the matter is clear,
in the Prophets, there are matters that are clear
and there are matters that are hidden,
as it is written: 'On that day
the mourning in Jerusalem will be great
like the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תורה's meaning was already clear, so its translation revealed nothing. The נביאים contain hidden passages, and translating them revealed those secrets.

steps.title: רב יוסף: without the תרגום we could not understand this פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the פסוק in זכריה cannot be understood without the תרגום. The תרגום explains that it refers to two separate mournings: for אחאב and for יאשיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If not for the translation of this פסוק, I would not know what it means. The תרגום says: On that day the mourning in ירושלים will be as great as the mourning for אחאב son of עמרי, whom הדדרימון son of טברימון killed in רמות גלעד, and like the mourning for יאשיהו son of אמון, whom Pharaoh the lame killed in the valley of מגידו.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף supports the previous answer by showing how the תרגום unlocks a פסוק that is otherwise impossible to understand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original פסוק seems to describe one mourning 'of הדדרימון in מגידון.' The תרגום splits it into two famous mournings: אחאב, killed by הדדרימון, and יאשיהו, killed in מגידו. This proves the תרגום of the נביאים revealed meaning that was hidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the תרגום is more than a word-for-word translation. It also carries the explanation of the פסוק.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
Were it not for the translation of this verse,
I would not know what it is saying:
On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be great
like the mourning for Ahab son of Omri
whom Hadadrimmon son of Tavrimon killed
in Ramoth-Gilead
and like the mourning for Josiah son of Amon
whom Pharaoh the lame killed
in the valley of Megiddo.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אִלְמָלֵא תַּרְגּוּמָא דְּהַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 15 that the נביאים contain hidden matters that the תרגום reveals.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the נביאים contain unclear passages that the translation exposes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's statement and the text of the תרגום on זכריה 12:11.

steps.title: Who were the men with דניאל who did not see the vision?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק in דניאל about men who were with him but did not see his vision, and asks who they were.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And I, דניאל, alone saw the vision, and the men who were with me did not see the vision, but a great fear fell on them and they ran away to hide.' Who were these men?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new related teaching about a hidden vision and asks who the men in the פסוק were. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching appears here because it comes from the same רבי ירמיה (or רבי חייא בר אבא), and it again involves חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי. The פסוק calls them 'men' without naming them, and the גמרא wants to know who they were.

phrases.english: 'And I, Daniel, alone saw the vision
and the men who were with me
did not see the vision
but a great trembling fell upon them
and they fled to hide themselves.'
Who were these men?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to another teaching from the same line of tradition, רבי ירמיה (or רבי חייא בר אבא), who taught about the תרגום in steps 5-6 and named חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי there. Its answer comes in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the unnamed men who were with דניאל.

steps.title: The men were חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה (some say רבי חייא בר אבא) says the men were the נביאים חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said, and some say it was רבי חייא בר אבא: These were חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the men with דניאל were three famous נביאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising. These were real נביאים, yet they could not see the vision that דניאל saw. That surprise leads to the next step, which explains how each side was greater.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said,
and some say it was Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba:
These are Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The men were חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי.

steps.title: Each side was greater than the other in a different way
steps.stepSummary: חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי were greater because they were נביאים and דניאל was not. דניאל was greater because he saw the vision and they did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were greater than him, and he was greater than them. They were greater than him because they were נביאים and he was not a נביא. He was greater than them because he saw the vision and they did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the topic by explaining how דניאל and the three נביאים each had an advantage over the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A beginner might ask: if they were נביאים, why could only דניאל see? The answer is that being a נביא means being sent to deliver ה׳'s message to the people. דניאל did not have that job, but he had a special ability to see hidden visions.
steps.whatToRemember: The translation of the נביאים shook the land because it revealed hidden meaning, while the תורה was already clear. דניאל was not a נביא, yet he saw a hidden vision that the נביאים חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי could not see.
steps.confusionAlert: Saying דניאל was 'not a נביא' does not mean he received no divine visions. It means he was not given the job of a נביא, who is sent to deliver ה׳'s message to the people.

phrases.english: They were greater than him,
and he was greater than them.
They were greater than him
because they were prophets and he was not a prophet.
He was greater than them
because he saw and they did not see.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינְהוּ עֲדִיפִי מִינֵּיהּ, וְאִיהוּ עֲדִיף מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the surprise created by step 18: real נביאים could not see what דניאל saw.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The נביאים were greater in their role as messengers. דניאל was greater in his ability to see hidden visions.

steps.title: If they did not see the vision, why were they afraid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the פסוק: the men with דניאל did not see the vision, yet the פסוק says they were seized with fear. Why would they be scared of something they never saw?
steps.simpleTranslation: But since they did not see it, why were they frightened?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem in the פסוק in דניאל. The men did not see the vision, yet they were terrified, which seems strange.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק says two things that seem to clash: the men did not see the vision, and a great fear fell on them. Fear usually comes from seeing something frightening. The גמרא wants to know what scared them.

phrases.english: But since they did not see [the vision],
phrases.notes: 'They' are חגי, זכריה and מלאכי from the step before.

phrases.english: what is the reason they were frightened?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּלָא חֲזוֹ, מַאי טַעְמָא אִיבְּעִיתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 19, which said the נביאים did not see the vision, and raises a difficulty from the rest of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the פסוק that the men did not see the vision
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If they saw nothing, there was no reason for them to be terrified and run away.

steps.title: Their guardian angels saw it
steps.stepSummary: The men did not see the vision themselves, but their מזל (spiritual guardian) did, so they sensed danger and became afraid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though they themselves did not see, their מזל saw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The men's spiritual guardians saw the vision, and that is why the men felt afraid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer separates the person from his מזל. Something can be perceived on a spiritual level even when the person's eyes see nothing. So both parts of the פסוק are true: they saw nothing, yet they felt fear.

keyTerms.meaning: A person's spiritual source or guardian angel

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִינְהוּ לָא חֲזוֹ,
phrases.english: Even though they themselves did not see,
their guardian angels saw.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִינְהוּ לָא חֲזוֹ, מַזָּלַיְיהוּ חֲזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the person versus his spiritual guardian
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Fear needs something the person sees himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מזל can see what the person cannot, and the person feels the fear.

steps.title: רבינא: Unexplained fear means your מזל sees something
steps.stepSummary: רבינא draws a general lesson: if a person suddenly feels afraid for no visible reason, his מזל sees a danger he cannot see.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Learn from this that when a person is suddenly frightened, even though he sees nothing, his מזל sees something.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא turns the story into a general rule for everyday life. Sudden fear without a reason is a sign of real danger that only the מזל sees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a שמע מינה, an inference from the story. What happened to the נביאים with דניאל applies to every person. It also prepares the next question: what should such a person do?

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can infer

phrases.english: Ravina said: Learn from this:
one who is frightened [for no clear reason],

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיהוּ לָא חָזֵי,
phrases.english: even though he does not see [anything],
his guardian angel sees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer of step 21 and makes it a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sudden unexplained fear means one's מזל perceives a real danger.

steps.title: What should such a person do?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what remedy a person has when he feels this kind of unexplained fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his remedy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question to set up the next step. If there is hidden danger, how does a person protect himself?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רבינא has said the fear signals real danger, the obvious next question is how to escape it. The answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: What is his remedy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical next step after רבינא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a frightened person can protect himself from the unseen danger

steps.title: Three remedies: קריאת שמע, moving away, or a protective saying
steps.stepSummary: He should say קריאת שמע. If he is in a filthy place where he may not say it, he should move four אמות away. If he cannot, he should say: 'The goat of the slaughterhouse is fatter than I am.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He should recite קריאת שמע. If he is standing in a filthy place, he should jump four אמות from his spot. If he cannot, he should say: 'The goat of the slaughterhouse is fatter than I.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the remedies in order. Each one is used only if the one before it is not possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קריאת שמע gives protection. In a מקום הטנופת one may not say holy words, so the backup is to move away from the dangerous spot. The last option is a saying that sends the harm elsewhere: if something must be struck, let it be the fat goat and not me.

keyTerms.meaning: A filthy place where holy words may not be said
Let him jump or move away

steps.whatToRemember: Sudden unexplained fear means one's מזל sees danger. The remedy is קריאת שמע, or moving four אמות away, or saying 'the goat of the slaughterhouse is fatter than I.'

phrases.english: He should recite Shema.
And if he is standing in a place of filth —
he should move four cubits from his place.
And if not — he should say this:
"The goat of the slaughterhouse is fatter than I."
phrases.notes: He means: let any harm land on the goat instead of me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 23 and ends the side discussion about fear.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A three-level remedy: קריאת שמע, then moving four אמות, then the protective saying.

steps.title: What does 'משפחה ומשפחה' come to teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the פסוק in אסתר. Since 'מדינה ומדינה ועיר ועיר' were already used for דרשות, what does 'משפחה ומשפחה' teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have said 'every province and every city' are for a דרשה, what does 'every family' come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The side discussion is over, and the גמרא returns to the פסוק in מגילת אסתר. It asks what the extra words 'משפחה ומשפחה' teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא (on 2b), 'מדינה ומדינה ועיר ועיר' were expounded to teach laws about the reading of the מגילה. Once those doubled words carry a דרשה, the doubled 'משפחה ומשפחה' in the same פסוק should also teach something. The גמרא asks what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it come to teach?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not connect this question to דניאל or the fear story. The גמרא has jumped back to the פסוק in אסתר (ט:כח) discussed earlier in the סוגיא, on 2b.

phrases.english: And now that you have said
"every province and every city" — are for exposition,
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier דרשה on 2b.

phrases.english: what does "every family" come to teach?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ מְדִינָה וּמְדִינָה וְעִיר וָעִיר לִדְרָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side story and goes back to the earlier דרשות on the פסוק in אסתר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What law the words 'משפחה ומשפחה' teach

steps.title: Even כהנים and לוים stop their service to hear the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא says 'משפחה ומשפחה' includes the families of כהונה and לויה. They stop their Temple service and come to hear the מגילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: It includes the families of כהונה and לויה, who stop their service and come to hear the reading of the מגילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא answers the question. 'Every family' includes even the כהנים and לוים, who leave their Temple work to hear the מגילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think Temple service is too important to interrupt. The extra word 'משפחה' teaches that every family, even those serving in the בית המקדש, must stop and hear the מגילה. This shows how important מקרא מגילה is.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that מקרא מגילה can push aside even עבודה in the בית המקדש. It becomes a key point in later discussions about which מצוות take priority.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
to include the priestly and Levitical families,
that they stop their service
and come to hear the reading of the Megilla.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא: לְהָבִיא מִשְׁפְּחוֹת כְּהוּנָּה וּלְוִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'משפחה ומשפחה' includes the families of כהונה and לויה, who stop their עבודה to hear the מגילה.

steps.title: רב: כהנים, לוים, and ישראל all stop to hear the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: Support from רב יהודה in the name of רב: the כהנים at their service, the לוים on their platform, and ישראל at their watches all stop and come to hear the מגילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The כהנים at their service, the לוים on their platform, and ישראל at their watches all stop their service and come to hear the reading of the מגילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רב to support רבי יוסי בר חנינא. It lists every group serving in the בית המקדש and says all of them stop to hear the מגילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's statement matches the דרשה and adds detail. It names three groups: כהנים doing the עבודה, לוים singing on the דוכן, and the ישראלים of the מעמד. Not one of them is exempt from hearing the מגילה.

keyTerms.meaning: רב יהודה quoting his teacher רב
The platform where the לוים sang in the בית המקדש
The group of ישראלים who stood by the עבודה on behalf of the nation

steps.whatToRemember: Hearing the מגילה is so important that כהנים, לוים, and ישראל in the בית המקדש all stop their service to hear it. The source is 'משפחה ומשפחה'.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Priests at their service
and Levites on their platform
and Israelites at their watches —
all of them stop their service
and come to hear the reading of the Megilla.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 26 with an אמורא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That the families of כהונה and לויה stop their עבודה to hear the מגילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of רב: כהנים, לוים, and ישראל all stop their service for מקרא מגילה

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the teaching about stopping Temple service
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same thing רב יהודה said: כהנים, לוים, and ישראל all stop their Temple duties to hear the מגילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: the כהנים at their service, the לוים on their platform, and ישראל at their watches all stop their service and come to hear the reading of the מגילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב יהודה said in the name of רב. This shows his teaching has an earlier source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 was a statement of an אמורא. Here the same rule appears in a ברייתא, which comes from the earlier תנאים. This gives the rule stronger backing, and it sets up the next step, which builds a new law on top of it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא), used to bring support

phrases.english: It was also taught this way (in a baraita):
The priests at their service,
and the Levites on their platform,
and the Israelites at their watches —
all of them stop their service
and come to hear the reading of the Megilla.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא with the same wording as רב יהודה's statement in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that those doing Temple service stop to hear the מגילה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same content.

steps.title: בית רבי learn that Torah study is also stopped for the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא, the scholars of בית רבי learn through a קל וחומר that people stop תלמוד תורה to hear the מגילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here, the scholars of the house of רבי relied on this to rule that people stop Torah study and come to hear the reading of the מגילה. This is a קל וחומר from Temple service: if we stop Temple service, which is very serious, then surely we stop Torah study.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars of בית רבי use the ברייתא to create a new rule: people also stop learning Torah to hear the מגילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is a קל וחומר. Temple service is treated as the 'stricter' activity, and even it is stopped. So Torah study, assumed to be less strict, is certainly stopped. The whole argument depends on that assumption, and the next step attacks it.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they relied (they based a ruling on this)
The court and students of רבי יהודה הנשיא

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical הלכה that we stop תלמוד תורה in order to hear the מגילה.

phrases.english: From here the members of the house of Rabbi relied
that one stops Torah study
and comes to hear the reading of the Megilla,
by an a fortiori argument from the Temple service:
Just as the service, which is stringent —
we stop it,
Torah study, is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new law from the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah study is interrupted to hear the מגילה, learned by קל וחומר from Temple service.

steps.title: Is Temple service really more important than Torah study?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the קל וחומר's assumption that Temple service is stricter than Torah study. It begins quoting a פסוק about יהושע at יריחו to show otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is Temple service really more serious than Torah study? Isn't it written: 'And it was when יהושע was by יריחו, he lifted his eyes and saw, and behold a man was standing opposite him... and he bowed down.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that Temple service outranks Torah study, and starts bringing a פסוק as proof. The full point of the proof comes in steps 35-37. First the גמרא takes a side detour about this פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If Torah study is actually greater than Temple service, the קל וחומר of בית רבי falls apart. The פסוק about the angel who came to יהושע is explained in steps 35-37 to show that Torah study is more important. For now, the גמרא only quotes the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (introduces a פסוק that challenges)

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not finished here. The גמרא pauses to discuss how יהושע could bow to the figure (steps 31-34). Only afterward, in steps 35-37, does it explain how this פסוק shows Torah study is greater.

phrases.english: And is the service more stringent than Torah study?
But isn't it written:
"And it was when Joshua was by Jericho
that he lifted his eyes and saw,
and behold, a man stood opposite him [etc.]
and he bowed down (on his face)."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the premise of the קל וחומר in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that עבודה is חמורה compared to תלמוד תורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק about יהושע and the angel will show that Torah study is greater than Temple service, which would undo the קל וחומר.

steps.title: How could יהושע bow to an unknown figure?
steps.stepSummary: A side question: רבי יהושע בן לוי forbids greeting an unknown person at night because it may be a שד, so how could יהושע bow to a stranger?
steps.simpleTranslation: How did he do this? Didn't רבי יהושע בן לוי say: a person may not greet his fellow at night, because we worry that maybe it is a שד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the main challenge to ask a side question about the פסוק itself. Why did יהושע bow to a figure he did not recognize?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that greeting an unknown figure at night is forbidden, since it might be a שד. Bowing is even more than greeting, so יהושע's action seems to contradict this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And how could he do this?

phrases.english: And how did he do this?
But didn't Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say:
It is forbidden for a person to give greeting
to his fellow at night,
we are concerned that perhaps it is a demon!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכִי עָבֵיד הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question on the פסוק quoted in step 30, before the main challenge is finished.
steps.kashyaTarget: יהושע's bowing to an unknown figure at night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע בן לוי forbids even greeting an unknown figure at night out of fear it is a שד.

steps.title: The figure said he was the captain of God's army
steps.stepSummary: יהושע's case was different, because the figure told him, 'I am the captain of the army of ה׳.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was different there, because he told him: 'I am the captain of the army of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the side question. יהושע knew who it was because the figure identified himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about a שד applies only when you do not know who the figure is. Here the figure said he was an angel of God, so יהושע was not bowing to an unknown being.

keyTerms.meaning: Captain of the army of God (an angel)

phrases.english: It is different there, as he said to him:
"For I am the captain of the host of the Lord."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יהושע bowed to an unidentified figure who might have been a שד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The figure identified himself as God's angel, so the concern did not apply.

steps.title: Maybe the שד was lying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: perhaps it was a שד who lied about being an angel?
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they lie?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. A שד could falsely claim to be an angel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Self-identification only helps if it can be trusted. If שדים can lie, saying 'I am God's captain' proves nothing.

phrases.english: But perhaps they lie?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reliance on the figure's claim to be an angel.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שד could lie about its identity.

steps.title: שדים do not say God's name for nothing
steps.stepSummary: There is a tradition that שדים do not use God's name in vain. So once the figure mentioned ה׳, יהושע knew it was a true angel.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have a tradition that they do not bring out the name of Heaven for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a שד would not falsely use God's name. This closes the side discussion about יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The figure did not just claim a title. He mentioned God's name, and by tradition שדים do not do that in vain. So יהושע could trust him and bow, and the גמרא can now return to its main challenge about Torah study versus Temple service.

keyTerms.meaning: We have a tradition (we learned it as received knowledge)
The name of Heaven, God's name

steps.whatToRemember: The side question is settled: יהושע could bow because the figure used God's name, which שדים do not do in vain. The main challenge (that Torah study may be greater than Temple service) is picked up again in step 35 and proven in step 37.

phrases.english: It is learned by tradition that they do not utter
the name of Heaven for nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמִירִי דְּלָא מַפְּקִי שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם לְבַטָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 33 and closes the side discussion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שד might lie and call itself God's angel.
steps.terutzMaskana: שדים do not use God's name in vain, so the claim was trustworthy.

steps.title: The angel lists two things יהושע neglected
steps.stepSummary: The angel tells יהושע that he neglected the afternoon תמיד earlier, and that he is neglecting תלמוד תורה now.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (the angel) said to him (יהושע): Earlier today you neglected the afternoon daily offering, and now you have neglected Torah study.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reveals why the angel appeared to יהושע: to rebuke him for two things that were neglected. This sets up the comparison that will show which one is more serious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two different kinds of מצוות are now placed side by side. One is Temple service (the תמיד), and the other is Torah study. Because both are on the table, the next lines can show which one the angel treats as more serious, and that is the proof the גמרא is building.

keyTerms.meaning: Yesterday or earlier. Here it refers to the afternoon that just passed, before night fell.
The afternoon daily offering brought every day.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yesterday you neglected
phrases.notes: The angel is talking to יהושע here, and 'yesterday' means the afternoon that just passed.

phrases.english: the afternoon daily offering,
and now you have neglected Torah study.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אֶמֶשׁ בִּטַּלְתֶּם תָּמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps 31 to 34 settled the side question of whether the figure was really an angel. This step returns to the main proof begun in Step 30 by explaining what the angel came to say.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge from Step 30 against the assumption that Temple service is stricter than Torah study.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The angel's words to יהושע at יריחו, based on the פסוק of 'שר צבא ה׳'.

steps.title: יהושע asks which sin the angel came about
steps.stepSummary: יהושע asks the angel which of the two neglected matters prompted his visit.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהושע said to him: For which of these two did you come?
steps.whatsHappening: יהושע asks a clarifying question: was the angel sent because of the missed offering, or because of the missed Torah study? This prepares the answer that will decide which one is more serious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angel's visit was a response to a sin. Whichever sin caused the visit must be the more serious one. So this question is exactly what turns the story into a proof.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: עַל אֵיזֶה מֵהֶן בָּאתָ?
phrases.english: He said to him: For which of these did you come?
phrases.notes: Now יהושע is speaking to the angel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: עַל אֵיזֶה מֵהֶן בָּאתָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The angel mentioned two sins in Step 35. יהושע now asks which one was the real reason for the visit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which neglected מצוה, the תמיד or תלמוד תורה, caused the angel to come.

steps.title: The angel answers: I came because of now
steps.stepSummary: The angel quotes his own words 'עתה באתי' ('I have come now'), showing that he came because of the neglect of תלמוד תורה happening right now.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Now I have come.' In other words, I came because of what you are neglecting now, which is Torah study.
steps.whatsHappening: The angel answers that he came because of the 'now' sin, the Torah study being neglected tonight. This is the heart of the proof against the earlier קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'עתה באתי' are from the פסוק itself (יהושע ה:יד). The word 'עתה' (now) connects to 'ועכשיו' (and now) from Step 35, which was about Torah study. So the angel was sent because of the missed Torah study, not the missed offering, and that shows Torah study is more serious than the תמיד.

keyTerms.meaning: Now I have come. These are words from the פסוק, read here as 'I came about the matter of now.'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'עתה באתי' as simply 'I just arrived.' The גמרא reads 'עתה' (now) as pointing back to 'ועכשיו' (and now), which was the neglect of תלמוד תורה. That reading is the whole proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source the גמרא uses to show that תלמוד תורה can be greater than Temple service. That idea undercuts the קל וחומר from earlier in the סוגיא.

phrases.english: He said to him: "Now I have come,"
phrases.notes: In other words: I came because of the present sin, the neglect of Torah study.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers יהושע's question from Step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The angel came because of the neglect of תלמוד תורה happening 'now.' This shows that Torah study outweighs the תמיד.

steps.title: יהושע immediately responds, and רבי יוחנן is introduced
steps.stepSummary: יהושע immediately corrects the problem, as the פסוק describes him spending that night 'in the midst of the valley.' רבי יוחנן is introduced to explain that phrase.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately, as it says: 'And יהושע lodged that night in the midst of the valley.' רבי יוחנן said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that יהושע acted right away to fix what the angel pointed out, and it quotes a פסוק about where he spent that night. Then it introduces רבי יוחנן, whose explanation of the phrase 'in the midst of the valley' comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'בתוך העמק' (in the midst of the valley) seems like simple geography. The גמרא is about to have רבי יוחנן read it as describing how יהושע fixed the sin. The line ends right as his explanation begins, so this step is a setup.

keyTerms.meaning: And he lodged, meaning he stayed overnight.
A valley. The word can also suggest depth.

steps.confusionAlert: The quoted פסוק is actually combined from two פסוקים (יהושע ח:ט and ח:יג). Do not look for these exact words together in one פסוק.

phrases.english: Immediately: "And יהושע lodged
that night
in the midst of the valley,"
phrases.notes: From יהושע ח:יג. This phrase is the one רבי יוחנן will explain.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד: וַיָּלֶן יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּלַּיְלָה הַהוּא בְּתוֹךְ הָעֵמֶק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the angel identifies the neglect of Torah study as the problem in Step 37, יהושע immediately responds, as the פסוקים describe.
steps.raayaObject: That יהושע understood the rebuke to be about Torah study and immediately fixed it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהושע ח:ט and ח:יג, about to be explained by רבי יוחנן.
